summary: Tested PATCH /api/auth/profile email update feature. All 6 backend tests PASS (login+me, name-only update, invalid=422, uniqueness=409, case-insensitive same-account=200, full update+relogin+revert). Frontend: email input is no longer disabled, type='email', onChange works, old helper text 'ne peut pas être modifié' removed, saving new email updates DB and /me reflects it, revert works. Bug is FIXED.

integration_issues.flow: Account email update — invalid email UX
integration_issues.issue: When user types an invalid email (e.g. 'foobar') and clicks Enregistrer, backend correctly returns 422 but the frontend does NOT surface any error message in [data-testid=account-name-msg]. Spec expected either a frontend regex guard ('Adresse e-mail invalide') OR the backend 422 detail to be rendered. formatError() should format Pydantic's array response, but the account-name-msg element is empty after the click. Recommend: add a client-side email regex check before submit + ensure the 422 detail array is rendered.

issues: Success message after email change reads only 'Profil mis à jour'. Spec/UX expects 'Profil et e-mail mis à jour' (or 'e-mail mis à jour') when the email field was changed, so the user has explicit feedback that their login identifier now differs. Minor copy tweak — logic works.

action_items: Optional: In Account.jsx saveName(), differentiate the success text when email changed (e.g. 'Profil et e-mail mis à jour').
Add client-side email regex validation (or ensure Pydantic 422 error surfaces in account-name-msg) so invalid emails show 'Adresse e-mail invalide' instead of a silent no-op.
critical_code_review_comments: Backend uniqueness check uses regex '^{new_email}$' with $options:'i' — since new_email is already lowercased and stored lowercased, a simple {"email": new_email} would be equivalent and safer (avoids regex-injection edge cases if email contained regex metacharacters, though EmailStr filters most). Not blocking.

After email update, the existing access_token cookie still contains the old email in the JWT payload — cosmetic only (server re-fetches user by sub id), but if any code path trusts token.email instead of DB, it could drift. Consider re-issuing cookies on email change.

success_rate.frontend: ~85% (core flow works; error UX minor gap)
